subject: Venus as the morning star, November 2026
query: what is the bright star in the eastern sky this morning
title: What is the bright star in the eastern sky this morning? It's Venus
answer: The very bright "star" low in the east before sunrise in November 2026 is the planet Venus. It is the brightest object in the predawn sky after the Moon, at about magnitude -4.5 to -4.7. Higher up, in the south-southeast, the bright point is Jupiter, with fainter, reddish Mars close beside it.
body:
Venus has returned to the morning sky as the "morning star." Astronomy magazine lists it at about magnitude -4.5 on Nov. 7 and -4.7 on Nov. 11, 2026, and says its backward (retrograde) motion against the stars ends on Nov. 11 at 10 a.m. EST. Through a telescope it currently shows a thin crescent, about 14% lit. In mid-November it sits roughly 15 degrees above the east-southeast horizon an hour before sunrise, close to Spica, the brightest star in Virgo. Mercury is also low in the east-southeast, to Venus's lower left.

Jupiter is the second-brightest point in the morning sky. It is high in the south-southeast before dawn in the constellation Leo, a few degrees from Regulus, Leo's brightest star. Mars has been closing in on Jupiter all autumn; the two pass about a degree apart, with the closest approach around Nov. 14 to 17 and the conjunction on Nov. 16, 2026. Mars looks much fainter and slightly orange.

The best time to look is about an hour before sunrise. Planets usually shine with a steadier light than stars, which tend to twinkle.
in_the_news: Venus became a brilliant morning star in early November 2026, while Mars and Jupiter meet in a close conjunction before dawn on Nov. 16.

faq.q: What is the bright planet in the east in the morning?
faq.a: Venus. In November 2026 it shines low in the east-southeast before sunrise.

faq.q: Is the morning star a star or a planet?
faq.a: The "morning star" is the planet Venus, not a star.

faq.q: What are the two bright objects close together before sunrise?
faq.a: High in the south-southeast, Jupiter and Mars, which pass about a degree apart around Nov. 14-17, 2026.

faq.q: When is the Mars and Jupiter conjunction in 2026?
faq.a: Nov. 16, 2026, in the morning sky in Leo.

faq.q: What is the bright star near Venus?
faq.a: Spica, the brightest star in the constellation Virgo.
